standard_prerequisites: The connection formula amuconnect (2.2), source line 675, for f0(x, lambda) in terms of f-infinity(x) and g-infinity(x) with theta-q-function coefficients; the theorem's proof substitutes lambda -> lambda-prime into it.

The Jacobi theta function theta_q and the q-Pochhammer symbols (a)-infinity, (q)-infinity appearing in the theta-coefficients; the proof uses only the pole positions of the auxiliary function C(x) and its periodicity C(xq)=C(x), both stated inside the span (source line 812).

The elementary elliptic-function argument that a q-periodic meromorphic function whose prescribed-pole residues vanish is constant, with the constant then read off at one further point (source lines 812-821).
core_obligations: For the generalized Zwegers mu-function of the source (Sections 1-2), the components satisfy the connection formula eq:tuchimi connection (2.4): f0(x, lambda-prime) = theta_q(lambda-prime) theta_q(a x/lambda-prime) x^alpha / (theta_q(lambda-prime/a) theta_q(x/lambda-prime) a) * f-infinity(x, lambda) - (a)-infinity (q)-infinity^2 * theta_q(-lambda-prime/(x lambda)) theta_q(-x) theta_q(-lambda lambda-prime/a) / (theta_q(x lambda) theta_q(lambda-prime/x) theta_q(lambda-prime/a) theta_q(a/lambda)) * g-infinity(x).
proof_roadmap: Substitute lambda -> lambda-prime in the known connection formula amuconnect (2.2) for f0(x, lambda): this produces the linear system eq:different variable (2.5) relating (f0(x, lambda-prime), f-infinity(x, lambda)) to (g0(x), g-infinity(x)) (source lines 797-801).

Eliminate g0(x) from the system (2.5): f0(x, lambda-prime) minus its f-infinity term equals a theta-coefficient times g-infinity(x); write the coefficient as (a)-infinity (q)-infinity^2 / theta_q(-a) * theta_q(-lambda-prime/(x lambda)) theta_q(-x) / (theta_q(x lambda) theta_q(lambda-prime/x)) * C(x) and record the explicit rational-in-theta expression of C(x) (source lines 802-811).

Pole-and-period argument: C(x) has only simple poles at x = q^j and x = (lambda-prime/lambda) q^j and satisfies C(xq) = C(x) (line 812); the residue at x = 1 vanishes by the explicit limit computation (lines 813-816), hence C(x) is constant in x (line 817); evaluating at x = -a/lambda gives C(x) = -theta_q(-a) theta_q(-lambda lambda-prime/a) / (theta_q(lambda-prime/a) theta_q(a/lambda)) (lines 819-821), which turns the C(x)-identity into the theorem's formula (2.4).
